title: U.S. House · Texas's 3rd District
area: Collin County and part of Denton County, in the northern Dallas suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Keith Self (R) defeated Mark Newgent in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. Evan Hunt won the Democratic primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Keith Self

summary.text: Keith Self is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Texas's 3rd Congressional District. A West Point graduate and retired Army lieutenant colonel, he served three terms as Collin County Judge before winning the seat in 2022. He advanced from the March 3, 2026 Republican primary and chairs the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1953. According to his official biography, he was born in a military hospital during his father's Army service, was raised in Texas and graduated from high school in Amarillo.
Earned an engineering degree from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1975 and a graduate degree from the University of Southern California in 1981.

Served in a 25-year Army career, according to his official biography, with tours as an Airborne Infantry platoon leader and company commander and as a Special Forces detachment and company commander. He deployed to Grenada, Bosnia, Afghanistan and Iraq, served at the Pentagon, and retired as a lieutenant colonel.
After the Army, he worked as a defense contractor.

Elected Collin County Judge, the county's chief administrative officer, in 2006, according to his official biography; he served three consecutive terms and retired from the office in 2018 (Ballotpedia lists his service as 2007 to 2018).

Placed in the top two in the March 1, 2022 Republican primary for Texas's 3rd District, which left the seat open after the incumbent, Van Taylor, advanced to a runoff and later withdrew. He won the November 8, 2022 general election and took office January 3, 2023.

Serves on the Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs, and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees), the Committee on Foreign Affairs (chairman of the Subcommittee on Europe; also on the Subcommittee on South and Central Asia) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Space and Aeronautics subcommittee).
His House website lists membership in the House Freedom Caucus and the Republican Study Committee, and as co-chair and founder of the Sharia-Free America Caucus.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Tracy, have been married since his West Point graduation; they live in McKinney and are active in their church and community.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Disability Assistance and Memorial Affairs and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees), the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Space and Aeronautics subcommittee), and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey or curated key-messages profile was found for Self in this race's coverage; positions on specific issues were not documented from the sources checked. Official sources give a 25-year Army career, while Ballotpedia lists service from 1975 to 2003, so Army dates are omitted.

candidates.name: Evan Hunt
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Evan Hunt is the Democratic nominee for Texas's 3rd Congressional District, a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and combat aviator who later worked in the defense and aerospace industry. According to his campaign website, he lives in McKinney and is running on health care costs, immigration reform, public education and campaign finance reform.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Pennsylvania with a double major in History and Political Science, including a year abroad at the London School of Economics, according to his campaign website. Ballotpedia lists the degree as 2002.

Joined the Air Force after September 11 and served as a B-1 bomber weapons systems officer and electronic warfare officer, with multiple combat deployments in support of Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation New Dawn, according to his campaign website. He also served as an instructor at the Air Force's Red Flag exercise.
Completed a master's degree in International Relations and Conflict Resolution at American Military University while in the Air Force (Ballotpedia lists 2009).

Continued in the Air National Guard in roles including Master Air Attack Plans Chief, Squadron Commander and Deputy Group Commander, and retired in 2022 as a lieutenant colonel with Meritorious Service Medals and Air Medals, according to his campaign website. Ballotpedia lists Air Force service from 2002 to 2022.

After active duty he held executive roles in the defense and aerospace industry, including at Raytheon, private equity-backed firms and venture-backed startups, according to his campaign website; Ballotpedia lists his profession as business development.
According to his campaign website, he has lived in Texas for over 11 years, the last six in McKinney, with his family; his son and daughter attend local public schools.
Was the only candidate in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary and became the nominee to face Rep. Keith Self.

priorities.text: Says he will push for federal investments in public schools, healthcare access, transportation, and infrastructure to keep pace with the district's rapid population growth.
Says he wants to start "getting big money out of our politics" by working to repeal Citizens United, instituting term limits, and preventing insider stock trading.

positions.summary: Supports federal investment to expand healthcare access, citing healthcare providers closing in the district.
positions.quote: That means fighting for federal investments in public schools, healthcare access, transportation, and infrastructure—investments that benefit the overwhelming majority of residents.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to affordable childcare as part of reducing cost pressures on working families.
positions.quote: We need to reduce the everyday cost pressures facing young and working families, starting with healthcare reforms, but also the construction of affordable housing, expanding access to affordable childcare, and preventing corporations from buying up entire neighborhoods of single-family homes and driving up prices.

positions.summary: Supports construction of more affordable housing and opposes corporate buyouts of single-family homes.
